messages:
emily (CS): Hey team — customer Acme reporting weird behavior from /v1/rerank. They POST a payload that mixes top-level `query`, a `documents` array (each with `passages`), and also a `candidates` list. Response is 200 but scores are all 0. Example they sent:
```json
{
  "query": "best onboarding FAQ",
  "documents": [
    {
      "id": "doc-1",
      "metadata": { "source": "kb" },
      "passages": [
        { "id": "p1", "query": "internal note", "text": "How to set up SSO" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    { "id": "cand-1", "text": "SSO guide short" },
    { "id": "cand-2", "text": "SSO troubleshooting" }
  ]
}
```
emily (CS): They say if they remove `documents` and send only `candidates` it returns non-zero scores. If they flatten passages into top-level candidates also works. They suspect naming collision because passages include an inner `query` field.

anita (Support): Repro report from customer attached. trace_id=trc-8f2a. Customer tried renaming root `query` -> `q` and still got zeros. Also tried sending `candidates` first then `documents` (order swapped) — same result. :grimacing:

anita (Support): Quick curl they ran: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \n  -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACTED' \n  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \n  -d '@payload.json'
```

derek (Eng-ML): Thanks — looks like an edge of our input normalization. Short summary from my side: our parser supports either `documents` (with nested `passages`) OR `candidates` as the canonical input, but if both are present we attempt to merge. There's a bug where if a nested passage contains a key named `query` it shadows the vectorization step and ends up producing empty feature vectors -> scores zero.

derek (Eng-ML): Can you paste the exact model param (model id & version) they're using? Also need the call headers (content-type + any special feature flags). I can repro locally with a minimal payload.

emily (CS): Model=redwood-open/fast-ranker:2025-11, no special headers except standard feature-flags: rerank-passages=true. I attached their sanitized payload.

jessica (Eng-API): Quick workaround: remove or rename inner `query` fields inside passages (e.g., `passage_query` or `note`) — that should avoid the shadowing. I'll add a validation in the API layer to reject mixed `documents`+`candidates` with a clear 400 and helpful message ("ambiguous input: supply only `documents` or `candidates`, or rename nested keys that conflict with top-level fields").

jessica (Eng-API): Repro steps for engineering: minimal failing payload below — reproduces 0 scores in my local run: 
```json
{
  "query": "rank these answers",
  "documents": [{ "id": "d1", "passages": [{ "id": "p1", "query": "note", "text": "A" }] }],
  "candidates": [{ "id": "c1", "text": "A" }]
}
```

derek (Eng-ML): Thanks, I can reproduce. Plan: hotfix to detect inner-key conflict + return 400 for mixed shapes in next 48h. Longer term: normalize and log a non-fatal warning if we auto-merge. For now CS please pass workaround to customer.

kyle (CS): Customer prefers not to change payload right away — asks for ETA. Derek, is 48h workable?

derek (Eng-ML): 48h is my target for the validation-only hotfix. If they need an immediate stopgap we can deploy a rule to treat inner `query` as `note` on the server side for that tenant (config flag) but that'll need ops signoff. cc @support-bot to open an internal ticket.

support-bot: Ticket created: #INC-2026 — assigned to eng-ml. ETA requested.

emily (CS): I'll share the workaround with Acme and escalate if they can't modify payload. Will follow up when the patch lands. :thumbsup:
